body: In the spirit of pushing forward a proposal, maybe you can investigate these ideas are propose some specific areas where we may want to use specific tools.

I definitely agree in exploring broad sets of mechanisms, but at their core, all of these mechanisms are still voting mechanisms. They just aggregate different types of votes.

Here are questions in general:
1. What is the sybil mechanism you use to protect against sybil voters.
2. In demarchy, you take a random sample according to what distribution? Is this resilient to individuals who can pose as 1/3 or 1/2 of all candidates.
3. I would like to think that Commonwealth can fit in at (4) to drive consensus decision making. One tenet of consensus decision making is having equal information to the issues at hand as well as cooperative discussion around them to drive better decision making.

If you're more interested in work like (3), look up "Robust Bayesian Truth Serum" as well as anything in the "peer-prediction mechanisms" literature. There is still the question when using subjective prediction markets of:
1. Who are the participants?
2. How do you prevent sybils?
